---
title: "Station health"
---

```{r}
source("_setup.R")
sp <- read_fig_csv("antenna_health_simulated_spells.csv")
```

Pulses per hour on each antenna port, every hour the receiver was up. Two rules run
over this:

- **Flat**: a port at zero pulses for 6 consecutive receiver-up hours. A silent port
  means a cable, dongle or antenna problem.
- **Hot**: a port above ten times its own median for 3 hours. A noise source.

Hours in which no port reported at all are receiver or power downtime and are reported
separately, not blamed on an antenna.

## What a fault looks like

This is a **simulated** receiver with three injected faults: port 3 dies on day 10,
port 2 has a noise burst on day 5, and the whole receiver is off for six hours on day 7.
The monitor flags exactly the first two. Simulated data is never uploaded to Motus.

![](figures/antenna_health_simulated.png)

```{r}
sp %>% transmute(Port = port, Type = type, Start = start, End = end, Hours = hours) %>% kable()
```

## Real data, with a caveat

Project downloads from Motus only carry pulse counts for hours in which a tag was
detected, so a missing hour is not evidence of a silent antenna. The flat flags on
this figure are therefore **not** faults. Reliable monitoring starts once the farm
receiver is registered and its own download includes every antenna-hour.

![](figures/antenna_health.png)
